pages.text: "A huge shell!" Dari set a soup-bowl-sized shell from the sandbar on the kitchen table. Hugging it in both flippers, he declared, "All for me!"
Mom approached with baby Kongal, who reached toward the shell. "Aaah!" "No! Mine!" Dari turned his back. Kongal pouted and cried.
Dari sat alone in a kitchen corner, hugging the shell. Kongal's crying was all he heard. Nothing felt fun. "Why am I unhappy with this huge shell?"
Mom sat beside him. "Such a big shell, but such a sad face?" Dari looked down. "It's big... but not fun at all."
Mom tapped the shell open. Two matching halves! "A shell has two halves. Share half, and it tastes twice as good." Dari's head rose. "Share half?"
Dari carried one half to Kongal's cradle. "I'm sorry. Let's eat together." Kongal stopped crying and bounced their round body.
"One, ask first! Kongal, want some?" Kongal flapped their flippers. "Two, share half!" Dari gave one half and held the other. Share half!
"Three, eat together!" Dari and Kongal ate. Kongal giggled. Much tastier together! Dari slapped his tail. His heart felt soft.
Now Dari knew the rules. "One, ask first! Two, share half! Three, eat together!" At dinner, he split a strand of seaweed first. "Together, Kongal!"
Mom hugged both children. "A wonderful big brother who knows how to share!" Sharing tasty food doubled smiles and joy. "Share half!" Dari gently poked Kongal's cheek.
